trigger: Three separate panels in one run returned a discrete-majority PASS carrying a dissenting lens's major defect (U01 iteration 1, U01 iteration 2, U07 iteration 2) — the L12 collision, which satisfies neither I16 nor I6 while DISAGREE is unavailable because a strict majority exists.
lesson: L12's collision is not a rare corner: it recurred three times in a single run, and in ALL THREE the narrow re-poll flipped the untested lenses to FAIL rather than confirming the majority. A majority PASS over a dissent's major is therefore weak evidence of correctness — it usually means the other lenses never tested that axis, not that they weighed and rejected it.
how_to_apply: Before treating a 2-1 PASS as settled, ASK each non-dissenting lens in writing whether it TESTED the disputed finding. If it did not, the narrow re-poll is legal under I41-4c and is usually decisive; if it did examine and decline, re-polling is vote-shopping and must not be done. Re-poll ONLY the untested lenses and ONLY about that finding, never the dissenter. Expect flips, and expect the re-polled lens to correct the dissent's framing while upholding its substance — that happened here and materially improved the repair brief.
